head: Samsung Call Screening may get cloud transcription in One UI 9.5
dek: Unfinished code in the One UI 9.5 beta, found in an Android Authority teardown, points to an opt-in "Cloud transcription" setting that would send incoming call audio to Samsung's servers for more accurate transcripts. Samsung hasn't announced it, and it can't be turned on yet.
details: Call Screening answers calls for you and shows a live transcript; since One UI 8.5 it runs fully on the phone, which keeps audio private but struggles with fast talkers and background noise. The code mentions English and Chinese first. On-device processing would stay the default, and the phone would fall back to it if the connection or Samsung's service drops. A first-use notice says the voice data would be used only to make the text transcripts.
where: Spotted in the One UI 9.5 beta on Galaxy phones; no release date, and it may not ship
means: If transcripts from screened calls come out garbled, a later update may offer a more accurate option, at the cost of sending call audio to Samsung.
todo: Nothing to do yet. If it arrives, it stays off unless you switch it on.
